verdict.rationale: Pylon's Connectors docs say an administrator can define Custom API tools that its agents use to hit internal or third-party API endpoints and take action outside Pylon. That is the product's own mechanism for agents to act through your APIs. Nothing documents per-action scoped auth, and nothing shows concrete refund, order or subscription flows. missing for 10: per-action scoped credentials/permissions for custom API tools, documented examples of transactional actions (refunds, order changes, subscription updates), approval/guardrail controls on agent actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the agent takes real actions through my APIs — refunds, order changes, subscription updates — with scoped auth per action

citations.quote: an administrator can define a Custom API tool that agents can use to hit internal or third party API endpoints
Connectors give Pylon agents access to external tools so they can search for context, retrieve information, and take action outside Pylon.
Support Agents can deflect customer questions using content, gather internal context for your team, and take action.
